question_text: A 21-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-week history of shortness of breath and dry cough. Eight weeks ago, she received a lung transplant from an unrelated donor. Current medications include prednisone, cyclosporine, and azathioprine. Her temperature is 37.8°C (100.1°F). Physical examination is unremarkable other than a well-healed surgical scar. Pulmonary function tests show a decline in FEV1 and FVC compared to values from several weeks ago. Histological examination of a lung biopsy specimen shows perivascular and interstitial lymphocytic infiltrates with bronchiolar inflammation. This patient's condition is most likely caused by T cell sensitization against which of the following?

        ### Question
